title: Prove sharp all-precision Neumann truncation at 226p² (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration. The scalar Neumann locality tail admits the smaller prescription

```diff
 g = 1/(16p), target tail < 2^(-16p)
-J = 512p²
+J = 226p² for every integer p >= 1
```

The coefficient 226 is optimal among nonnegative integer coefficients in `J=c p²` required to work for every positive precision. Coefficient 225 fails at p=1. The uniform proof uses a four-term binomial bound and geometric induction; sixteen direct cases corroborate its constants. This extends Jose Manuel's PR #3851 and James Reed's PR #3864 without replaying their results as the contribution. No new κ or selected-frontier change.

## Evidence

Before: PR3851 uses 512p² and PR3864 checks that coefficient for precisions 101–200 and at precision 1. After: a written all-positive-precision proof for 226p², exact integer exclusion of 225, sixteen full-tail comparisons using both integers and fractions, and four calibration-domain rejection controls.

From the repository root, with CPython 3.12.15 and the standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/optimal-neumann-quadratic-tail/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/optimal-neumann-quadratic-tail/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/optimal-neumann-quadratic-tail
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/optimal-neumann-quadratic-tail --check-source-history
```

All passed locally. Direct normal and optimized checks took 0.08 and 0.09 seconds; registered replay took 0.41 seconds on the first measured run. Output includes `PASS_OPTIMAL_NEUMANN_QUADRATIC_TAIL coefficient=226 excluded=225 direct_precisions=16 domain_controls=4 no_new_kappa`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` for all five files and the declared source-history commit. Optimized replay also passed in a standalone copy outside Git. Generated hash-bound receipt creation and refusal to overwrite an occupied receipt passed.

## Limitations

The same contraction and prefactor are hypotheses. The proof does not establish rounded evaluation, physical costs, inverse-norm assumptions, caller integration, complete outer tensor or integer recovery. The p=1 obstruction does not establish optimality on the production domain p>=101. No Gaussian/native replay, Lean, Docker or independent human/formal-kernel review is claimed.

## Open next questions

- Determine the smallest integer coefficient restricted to p>=101, beginning with monotonicity of the normalized logarithmic tail.
- Integrate the smaller J and path margins into the exact PR3851 caller while retaining every setup, rounding, routing and ownership obligation.

## Related open work

The refreshed open-work list contains no PR studying this same scalar tail or quadratic coefficient. Adjacent contributions have distinct hypotheses and quantities:

- #5150 proves the sharp inverse-norm order at broad Gaussian phase-cell edges. This grants a fixed contraction and prefactor; it does not derive that inverse estimate or compare its constants.
- #5153 proves an endpoint-conditioned coefficient-rounding guard for finite words. This bounds an exact scalar truncation tail and leaves rounded evaluation open; no numerical comparison is claimed.

PR #3851 and PR #3864 are merged predecessors. The ongoing Gaussian caller work in Discussion #4202 retains separate operator, rounding and global-reference obligations; this scalar theorem does not discharge them.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. Only the new research package is added; no caller, shared code or selected result is changed.
